description: Adjudication of the comparators' own metrics and datasets, plus two new measurements: a direct junction-resolution accuracy for all four methods, and an ablation that replaces PLECTA's exact per-junction maximum-weight matching with greedy cheapest-edge-first acceptance and changes nothing else.

statistics.kind: density-stratified paired percentile bootstrap, scene pairing preserved
statistics.applies_to: aggregate paired differences only; per-density cells are plain means

metric_adjudication.note: None of the five names the author supplied appears verbatim in either vendor tree. Each is matched below to the function that computes it, read from the vendored source rather than from the papers' prose.

jaccard.definition: TP/(TP+FP+FN) over pixels, after greedy consume-once matching of predicted mask pixels to reference skeleton pixels at radius 0, then 1, 2, 3
jaccard.reason: The test mask is not thinned before matching, so every extra pixel of mask thickness counts as a false positive against a 1-px reference. On the degraded mask it reports JI 0.564 where the same quantity computed on centrelines reports 0.919. It measures thickness, not tracing error. The correct form of the same idea -- tolerant completeness/correctness/quality -- is adopted instead.

FC.vendor_source: two different quantities carry this name. Pixel form: dataUtils.py::calcDiff line 870 (`perC = count/correctC*100`). Instance form: dataUtils.py::identification_LAP lines 562-605, pooled as the column 'FS coverage' in noise001/pool_data.py line 414
FC.definition: pixel form = tolerant recall of the reference centreline; instance form = fraction of each true line's length covered by the filament matched to it
FC.verdict: ADOPT THE PIXEL FORM, FOR MASK QUALITY ONLY
FC.reason: As a method metric it does not discriminate: 0.877-0.925 across all four methods on the degraded mask and 0.968-0.996 on the clean one, because methods grouping the same mask cover the same pixels. As a mask metric it is exactly the tolerant recall (completeness) the author wanted, and that is how it is reported here.

FFR.vendor_source: dataUtils.py::calcDiff line 872 (`FP_trueimg = FP/correctC*100`); instance form is the 'ratio no overlap' column, pool_data.py lines 386-388
FFR.definition: false pixels (or detections) divided by the REFERENCE length (or count), not by the prediction's own
FFR.reason: Not a rate: unbounded above, 0.628 on the degraded mask where tolerant precision is 0.998. The instance form is 0.00-0.05 for every method here and carries no signal. Tolerant precision (correctness) is the bounded, symmetric replacement.

FMC.vendor_source: no function of this name exists. The quantity is pool_data.py's 'ratio true defined', lines 383/406 (`len(unique match index)/len(unique true index)`), built on the Hungarian assignment in dataUtils.py::identification_LAP line 579
FMC.definition: fraction of reference filaments matched one-to-one to some distinct detection
FMC.verdict: DO NOT ADOPT -- IT INVERTS THE RANKING
FMC.reason: Saturated and anti-correlated with quality here: DNAi 0.993 and the greedy baseline 0.992 against PLECTA 0.982 on the degraded mask, while their pairwise F1 is 0.343 and 0.676 against 0.822. It counts existence, not correctness -- a method that halves every filament still offers a distinct detection per filament.

joinF1.vendor_source: dnai_comparison/vendor/DNAi/dnafiber/metric.py::DNAFIBERMetric, lines 9-343 (greedy IoU matching 126-156, detection F1 317-327, shipped IoU threshold 0.1 at line 39)
joinF1.definition: instance-detection F1 after greedy highest-IoU one-to-one matching of predicted to reference objects
joinF1.verdict: ADOPT AS A SECONDARY COMPANION, AT IoU 0.1 ONLY
joinF1.reason: It is the less harsh reading of instance quality the author wanted, it preserves the published ranking on all four methods in both mask conditions, and it is the one metric a reader from the DNA-fibre literature will recognise. At IoU 0.5 it is not stable -- PLECTA scores 0.439 on the degraded mask and 0.311 on the clean one, an inversion driven by instance length, not quality -- so only the shipped 0.1 threshold is reported.

tolerant_centreline_precision.verdict: ALREADY COVERED -- DO NOT DEFINE A NEW ONE
tolerant_centreline_precision.reason: It is `correctness` in the completeness/correctness/quality triple adopted here, and it is already implemented in comparisons/real_sem_study/scripts/graft_metrics.py::jaccard in all but name. Defining a fourth variant would add a definition to the paper without adding a measurement.

add.name: junction-resolution accuracy (exact rate + chance-corrected resolution index)
add.why: states the paper's central claim directly, separates all four methods, and is a decomposition of the primary metric rather than a second exam

add.name: tolerant centreline completeness / correctness / quality at tol = 2 px
add.why: the honest form of GraFT's Jaccard/FC/FFR; reports the input mask independently of any grouping method, which is what the mask-vs-method question needs

add.name: instance-detection F1 at IoU 0.1 (DNAi's own measure)
add.why: optional companion; a less harsh, familiar reading that preserves the ranking

reject: pairwise Jaccard (a monotone transform of the reported pairwise F1: F1 = 2J/(1+J), so it cannot change any ranking)
a newly defined tolerant centreline precision
recommended_metric_set.page_budget: two additions, both single numbers per method; the third is optional and can live in the supplement

graft.licence: MIT, (c) 2023 Isabella Osterlund -- covers the whole tree, including the bundled data files

bundled_real_data.why: Arabidopsis actin microscopy with no reference labelling of any kind. It can only be used the way the existing GraFT study already uses it -- to prove the import is faithful against GraFT's own output -- not to score anybody.

bundled_synthetic_data.why: the CSV carries per-pixel (line_no, x, y), i.e. instance labels with crossings, for one 500x500 frame of 10 filaments. Converted, scored and reported here.

public_dataset_cited.why: raw imagery only; no filament-level reference exists, so no method can be scored on it.

bundled_data.why: a single unlabelled smoke-test image; the training data path in configs/config.yaml is a private local directory (/home/clement/Documents/data/DNAFiber/...).

public_dataset_cited.content: software archive of the repository, not a dataset

dnai.domain_blocker: DNA fibre assays are two-colour: DNAi's own matcher weights colour continuity at weight_color = 1.0, equal to its angle term. Its reference annotation is per-fibre red/green tract length, not an instance mask with crossings. Scoring an overlap-aware instance method there would require inventing the reference the domain does not produce.
